answer: Honest participants harbor reputation across epochs, and peers slash any identity caught reusing seeds, making each fake account provably more expensive than its payoff. Each agent stakes collateral locked to a rotating beacon that publishes epoch seeds; identities must solve a unique proof-of-work tied to that seed, so mass-registering sybils hits a cost nadir where forged identities exceed expected rewards. From qwe0005's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
